version.changelog:
- Added required environment variables to metadata: GUARDIAN_AGENT, GUARDIAN_REVIEWER_B_AGENT, GUARDIAN_REPO, GUARDIAN_AUTO_MERGE, GUARDIAN_AUTO_FIX, GUARDIAN_MAX_PRS, GUARDIAN_MAX_ISSUES.
- Included 'openclaw' as a required bin in metadata.
- Updated documentation to reflect these additional required environment variables.
- No behavioral or logic changes to review or triage flow.

llm.summary: Repo Guardian is a disclosed GitHub PR automation skill, but it can auto-merge pull requests by default using model decisions on untrusted PR content.

dimensions.detail: GitHub API access and model-provider transmission of PR diffs are expected for the purpose, but write-capable repository access is risky because auto-merge defaults to true in the script and documentation is contradictory about whether merge is opt-in.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill includes disclosed manual and cron-based execution instructions and requires openclaw, python3, curl, and GH_TOKEN; it does not install hidden services or fetch remote executable code.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The script embeds PR titles, branch names, file names, and diffs into reviewer prompts, then treats model APPROVE verdicts as enough to merge, without a deterministic prompt-injection boundary, CI/status validation, or human approval gate.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Cron scheduling and memory trace logging are disclosed, but scheduled unattended operation combined with repository write actions and auto-merge creates a material review concern.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose includes PR review, comments, and auto-merge, which matches the script, but the capability is high impact because it can post GitHub comments and squash-merge PRs with the supplied GH_TOKEN.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with unattended repository write actions. Use a fine-grained token limited to one repository, set GUARDIAN_AUTO_MERGE=false or pass --no-merge unless a human approval process exists, configure two genuinely separate reviewers, and rely on GitHub branch protections and CI rather than model consensus alone.
llm.findings:
[PE3] expected: GH_TOKEN use is expected for GitHub API calls and the script requires it explicitly rather than reading local auth stores; the concern is token scope, not credential theft evidence.
[SC2] expected: The cited curl calls access GitHub API endpoints for PRs, comments, issues, and merge operations; I found no remote script download or execution in the artifact.
[LP3] unexpected: The skill lacks a tight tool/permission boundary while using shell commands and repository write authority, which matters because it can merge PRs.
[RA2] expected: The cron behavior is documented and user-configured, not hidden persistence, but scheduled unattended execution increases the impact of any misconfiguration.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Issue triage is advertised, but the script only fetches and counts issues and says auto-fix processing is not implemented.
[E1] expected: Posting comments to GitHub and sending PR diffs to configured OpenClaw model agents are disclosed data flows; I did not find token exfiltration in comment bodies or prompts.
[SDI-4] unexpected: The fallback comment/logs imply a distinct fallback model, but the code retries the same Reviewer B agent.
[T01] unexpected: The prompt-injection risk is artifact-backed: untrusted PR content is placed directly in model prompts and model output can authorize a merge.
[T09] unexpected: The unsafe default is artifact-backed: guardian.sh sets GUARDIAN_AUTO_MERGE to true when unset, while the Safety section says auto-merge is disabled by default.
